newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG, MAGONI SHARE VICTORY IN WOMEN'S SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG, MAGONI SHARE VICTORY IN WOMEN'S SLALOM.

text.p: Overall champion Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden and Lara Magoni of Italy finished in a dead heat in Sunday's slalom to share victory in the last race of the women's World Cup season.
Wiberg, fifth after the first run and 0.76 of a second behind pace-setter Magoni, blistered the 55-gate course with a sizzling second run of 48.30 seconds to jump into the lead.

Magoni, the silver medallist in slalom at the Sestriere world championships, rose to the occasion as the last racer down the mountain by clocking 49.06 for a combined time of one minute, 35.77 seconds to tie slalom champion Wiberg for first.
It was the first time in World Cup history that a slalom ended in a tie.
Katja Seizinger of Germany finished third, 0.54 of a second behind the co-winners.
The shared victory capped off an outstanding season for Wiberg, who won the slalom title and finished third in the Super-G standings.
The vivacious Swede, who won seven races this season, triumphed in the downhill at the World Cup Finals to become the only active woman racer with victories in all four events.
"It was a great way to end the season," said Wiberg. "I said to myself before the second run, 'All right, I'm going to end the season the way I'd like.'
"It's going to be hard to do as well next year but I will try. But I lost the Super-G title (despite leading the standings going into the final race) so I have something more to shoot for."
First place was a thrilling first for late-bloomer Magoni.
The 28-year-old Italian had never made it to the podium before this season but has now done so five times -- including a world championship silver in the slalom at Sestriere.
"At the beginning of the season I was so disappointed, I wasn't sure I would keep on racing and now I finish like this," said Magoni.
Fourth place went to Ingrid Salvenmoser of Austria in 1:36.97, followed by Norway's Trine Bakke and World Cup giant slalom champion Deborah Compagnoni of Italy in sixth.
New Zealander Claudia Riegler, winner of three slaloms this season, held on to second place ahead of Compagnoni in the season slalom standings by finishing ninth in 1:37.72.
